data.description:
Deine Aufgaben

Stell dir Flotten autonomer Gabelstapler vor, die jeweils mehrere Tonnen wiegen und schwere Lasten in bis zu 14 Meter hohe Regale heben, sicher, rund um die Uhr und in unmittelbarer Nähe von Menschen. Genau das entwickeln wir bei Jungheinrich Robotics. Dabei spielt KI-gestützte Softwareentwicklung eine wichtige Rolle. In dieser Position trägst du dazu bei, dass sich jedes dieser Fahrzeuge genau so bewegt, wie es soll.

Wir suchen Verstärkung sowohl auf Senior- als auch auf Staff-Level. Bewirb dich auf die Position, die am besten zu dir passt, und gemeinsam finden wir die richtige Rolle für dich!

  • Du entwickelst und verantwortest Komponenten unserer Steuerungssoftware für autonome Gabelstapler, von der Hardware-Abstraktionsschicht und der Aktuatorsteuerung auf Basis von ros_control/ros2_control bis hin zu den Schnittstellen zur Lokalisierung und Navigation.
  • Du modellierst und implementierst die Fahrzeugkinematik für unterschiedliche Gabelstaplertypen, einschließlich beschleunigungs- und ruckbegrenzter Bewegungsabläufe.
  • Du integrierst Motorsteuerungen, Antriebe und Aktuatoren über Feldbussysteme, insbesondere CANopen.
  • Du integrierst und kalibrierst Robotersensoren, darunter Encoder, IMUs, Laserscanner, Kameras und Hubhöhensensoren.
  • Du verbesserst die Zuverlässigkeit unserer Roboter im realen Einsatz durch intelligente Fehlerbehandlung, automatische Wiederherstellungsmechanismen sowie Logging- und Analysetools.
  • Du definierst und führst Integrations- und Systemtests an realen Robotern, Prüfständen und in Simulationen durch.
  • Du nutzt KI-gestützte Entwicklungstools in deinem Arbeitsalltag, von der Programmierung und Testgenerierung bis hin zur Loganalyse.
  • Du gestaltest technische Konzepte und die Weiterentwicklung unserer Steuerungsarchitektur mit und unterstützt weniger erfahrene Kolleg:innen.

Dein Profil

  • Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Studium in Elektrotechnik, Mechatronik, Informatik, Robotik oder einem vergleichbaren Bereich oder bringst entsprechende praktische Erfahrung mit.
  • Du bringst mindestens 4 Jahre Berufserfahrung in der Robotik-Softwareentwicklung mit, davon mindestens 2 Jahre in der Arbeit mit realen mobilen Robotern.
  • Du nutzt KI-basierte Tools, wie beispielsweise Coding-Assistenten, aktiv in deinem Arbeitsalltag und möchtest deren Einsatzmöglichkeiten weiter ausbauen.
  • Du verfügst über ein fundiertes Verständnis der Kinematik mobiler Roboter, einschließlich beschleunigungsbegrenzter Bewegungen, sowie des Zusammenspiels von Lokalisierung, Navigation und Hardware.
  • Du bringst fundierte Erfahrung mit ROS1/ROS2 oder vergleichbarer Middleware sowie mit ros_control/ros2_control oder ähnlichen Frameworks mit.
  • Du hast Erfahrung in der Integration von Sensoren, Aktuatoren und Feldbussystemen, idealerweise CANopen.
  • Du verfügst über sehr gute Programmierkenntnisse in C++ und solide Kenntnisse in Python. Erfahrung mit Rust ist ein Plus.
  • Du begeisterst dich dafür, mit deiner Software mehrere Tonnen schwere autonome Fahrzeuge sicher und präzise zu bewegen, und möchtest die Zukunft großer Roboterflotten in realen Lagerumgebungen mitgestalten.
  • Du bringst idealerweise vertiefte Kenntnisse in mindestens einem der folgenden Bereiche mit:
    • Sicherheitsgerichtete SPS-Anwendungen, beispielsweise Siemens S7 / TIA Portal Safety, Beckhoff TwinSAFE oder SICK Flexi Soft.
    • Hardware-nahe Softwareentwicklung, beispielsweise CAN-Treiber, PROFINET, Timing und Synchronisation in Sensornetzwerken, idealerweise mit Kenntnissen im Bereich Mikrocontroller und Embedded Systems.
    • Autonome Software für reale Roboter, beispielsweise Lokalisierung, Navigation und Bewegungsplanung, kombiniert mit dem Interesse, dein Wissen im Bereich Low-Level-Control weiter zu vertiefen.
  • Du bringst idealerweise Erfahrung mit ruckbegrenzten Bewegungsabläufen, dem Aufbau vollständiger Software-Stacks für mobile Roboter oder Intralogistik-Anwendungen mit automatisierten Gabelstaplern, AGVs oder AMRs mit.
  • Du kommunizierst fließend auf Englisch und verfügst über Deutschkenntnisse auf mittlerem Niveau (mindestens B1).
  • Du bist bereit, vor Ort an unserem Standort in München zu arbeiten.

Was wir bieten

  • Spitzentechnologie: Als Pioniere der Robotik sind wir in der Lage, ohne Schienen und Leitlinien zu navigieren und zu manipulieren, und bieten Lösungen für Prozesse, die noch nie jemand zuvor automatisieren konnte!
  • Team: Wir sind ein internationales Team mit mehr als 25 Nationalitäten. Du wirst in einem Team mit sehr smarten, bescheidenen, kooperativen und fleißigen Individuen arbeiten.
  • Kultur: Sei einfach Du selbst! Werde Teil eines dynamischen, innovativen und vielfältigen Teams, das Zusammenarbeit über Hierarchie stellt. Um innovativ zu sein, muss man ab und zu scheitern – wir lernen und verbessern uns ständig.
  • Arbeitsplatz: Unser Büro befindet sich in der Nähe der S‑Bahn-Station „Hirschgarten“. Wir arbeiten in einem Büro im Loft-Stil mit toller Ausstattung, eigener Werkstatt und Testbereich.

data.title: Staff Robotics Software Engineer (w/m/d)

data.description:
Your tasks

Imagine fleets of autonomous forklifts, each weighing several tons, lifting heavy loads into racks up to 14 meters high, safely and around the clock, right next to people. That's what we build at Jungheinrich Robotics, and AI-assisted engineering plays an important role in how we do it. In this role, you help ensure that every one of these vehicles moves exactly as intended.

We are hiring at both Senior and Staff levels. Apply for the role that fits you best, and we'll find the right fit together!

  • You develop and take ownership of control software components for our autonomous forklifts, from the hardware abstraction layer and actuator control based on ros_control/ros2_control to the interfaces with localization and navigation.
  • You model and implement vehicle kinematics for different forklift types, including acceleration- and jerk-limited motion.
  • You integrate motor controllers, drives, and actuators using fieldbus systems, particularly CANopen.
  • You integrate and calibrate robot sensors, including encoders, IMUs, laser scanners, cameras, and lift height sensors.
  • You improve the reliability of our robots in real-world environments through intelligent error handling, automated recovery mechanisms, and logging and analysis tools.
  • You define and execute integration and system-level tests on real robots, test benches, and in simulation.
  • You use AI-assisted engineering tools in your daily work, from coding and test generation to log analysis.
  • You contribute to technical concepts and the development of our control architecture while supporting less experienced colleagues.

Requirements

  • You hold a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field, or bring equivalent practical experience.
  • You bring at least 4 years of professional experience in robotics software development, including at least 2 years working with real mobile robots.
  • You actively use AI-based tools, such as coding assistants, in your daily work and are eager to explore their potential further.
  • You have a solid understanding of mobile robot kinematics, including acceleration-limited motion, and how localization and navigation interact with the hardware.
  • You bring solid experience with ROS1/ROS2 or comparable middleware, as well as ros_control/ros2_control or similar frameworks.
  • You have experience integrating sensors, actuators, and fieldbus systems, ideally CANopen.
  • You have strong programming skills in C++ and solid knowledge of Python. Experience with Rust is a plus.
  • You are passionate about developing software that enables heavy autonomous vehicles to move smoothly and safely, and want to help shape the future of large robotic fleets in real warehouse environments.
  • You ideally bring in-depth expertise in at least one of the following areas:
    • Safety PLC applications, such as Siemens S7 / TIA Portal Safety, Beckhoff TwinSAFE, or SICK Flexi Soft.
    • Low-level, hardware-related software development, including CAN drivers, PROFINET, timing, and synchronization in sensor networks, ideally combined with microcontroller or embedded systems knowledge.
    • Autonomous software for real robots, such as localization, navigation, and motion planning, combined with an interest in developing deeper expertise in low-level control.
  • You ideally have experience with jerk-limited motion, setting up complete mobile robot software stacks, or intralogistics applications involving automated forklifts, AGVs, or AMRs.
  • You communicate fluently in English and have intermediate German language skills (B1 level or higher).
  • You are willing to work on-site at our Munich location.

What we have to offer

  • Cutting-edge technology: As pioneers in robotics we can navigate and manipulate without rails and guides and offer solutions to processes that no one could automate ever before!
  • Team: We are an international team with more than 25 nationalities. You’ll work in a team with exceptionally smart, humble, collaborative and hardworking individuals.
  • Culture: Come as you are! Join a vibrant, inventive, and diverse team that values collaboration over hierarchy. To innovate you need to fail from time to time — we always learn and improve.
  • Workplace: Our office is located near the S‑Bahn station “Hirschgarten”. We work in a loft-style office with great equipment, our own workshop and testing area.
  • Full Board: You don’t feel like thinking about what you want to have for lunch tomorrow, not to mention preparing it? Luckily, our french cook treats us with a freshly cooked free lunch everyday! And as the cherry on top, there is a packed fridge with drinks, fresh fruits and of course coffee!
  • Flexibility: Flexibility is a top priority for us. Our hybrid working model for positions where presence is dispensable helps to achieve a healthy work-life balance.
  • Benefits: We offer attractive holiday, EGYM, health care, and compensation packages. Learn more about our current benefits here.

Not sure if you meet every single requirement? That's okay. We know that great people don't always tick every box. If you're excited about the opportunity to help shape the future of robotics and believe you can make an impact, we'd love to hear from you. Your experience may be a great fit for this role or another opportunity at Jungheinrich Robotics.

At Jungheinrich Robotics, where Magazino GmbH found its place, fostering inclusivity is very important to us. We are dedicated to create an inclusive environment for all candidates and provide equal opportunities to all qualified applicants regardless of gender, ethnicity, age, national origin, sexual orientation, culture, or education. If you need any reasonable adjustments to make the application process accessible for you, we’ll do our best to accommodate you. Feel free to approach us for that!

Senior Performance Marketing Manager Google Ads (m/w/d)

Du führst ein eigenes Portfolio aus 6–7 D2C-Marken — nur Google Ads, mit eigenem AI-Dev-Team im Rücken und monatlichem Bonus auf deine Leistung.

Google Ads können viele — bei uns zeigst du, was einen Spezialisten ausmacht. Die stärksten D2C-Marken holen Performance-Marketing immer öfter ins eigene Haus. Eine Agentur wird da nur noch gebraucht, wenn sie besser ist als das Inhouse-Team: tiefer im Kanal, schneller in der Steuerung, mit Werkzeugen, die dort niemand hat.

Genau dafür gibt es Touchpoint. Wir machen ausschließlich Google Ads, steuern über 100 Mio. € Werbebudget im Jahr und arbeiten für Marken wie Snocks, BLACKROLL, BIKE24 und TEVEO. Als Senior übernimmst du nach der Einarbeitung ein eigenes Portfolio von sechs bis sieben dieser Kunden — von der Kontostrategie bis zum Gespräch mit deren Performance-Team.

Was es hier leichter macht als anderswo: vier Entwickler bauen AI- und Automations-Tools nur für unser Marketing-Team, wir haben ein eigenes CSS, echte Attribution und steuern Budgets mehrmals täglich. Weniger Fleißarbeit, mehr Strategie — und über den monatlichen Bonus verdienst du direkt an dem mit, was du aus deinem Portfolio machst.

Warum es diese Rolle gibt

Touchpoint wächst — bisher vor allem aus den eigenen Reihen: Werkstudierende werden Junioren, Junioren werden Seniors. Das funktioniert, ist aber langsamer als die Nachfrage unserer Kunden. Deshalb holen wir jetzt erfahrene Google-Ads-Leute von außen dazu.

Gleichzeitig verändert sich, wie wir arbeiten: AI-Workflows und unser Remote-Setup entstehen gerade. Wer jetzt kommt, übernimmt nicht nur Kunden, sondern gestaltet mit, wie Touchpoint in zwei Jahren arbeitet.

Was du bewegen wirst

Nicht als Aufgabenliste, sondern als das, was nach den ersten Monaten anders ist:

  • Dein Portfolio läuft. Nach sechs bis acht Wochen Einarbeitung verantwortest du sechs bis sieben D2C-Kunden selbst — Kampagnenstruktur, Gebotsstrategie, Budgetverteilung und Tests entscheidest du allein.

  • Shopping, PMax und Feed sitzen. Deine Konten liefern die Performance, die versprochen wurde. Und wenn nicht, sprichst du es beim Kunden an, bevor er fragt.

  • Du bist Sparringspartner, nicht Dienstleister. Mit den Inhouse-Teams deiner Kunden legst du Budget, Richtung und Roadmap fest — und hältst fachlich dagegen, wenn es nötig ist.

  • Deine Kunden bleiben und wachsen. Zufriedenheit misst jeder Kunde monatlich mit — und dein Portfolio wächst im Bestand.

  • Das Team wird besser durch dich. Du arbeitest mit Junioren an gemeinsamen Cases, gibst Feedback und schließt Wissenslücken.

Wie hier gearbeitet wird

Bei uns zählt Drive mehr als ein perfekter Lebenslauf. Fachliche Lücken lassen sich schließen — der Wille, besser zu werden, nicht.

  • Ehrlich zum Kunden: Wenn es für ihn besser ist, raten wir auch mal zur Pause.

  • 80 % richtig schlägt 20 % perfekt. Exzellenz heißt bei uns nicht Perfektion, sondern höchster Standard bei jedem Kunden.

  • Feedback in beide Richtungen, mit festen Formaten: monatlicher Puls-Check, Quartalsfeedback an die Geschäftsführung, Ergebnisse im All-Hands.

  • Alle zählen gleich — ob Werkstudent:in oder Senior. Prozesse passen wir so an, dass das ganze Team davon profitiert.

Wen wir suchen

Jemand, der Google Ads für E-Commerce nicht nur kann, sondern lebt — und Kunden gern selbst führt.

Das brauchst du auf jeden Fall

  • Mindestens drei Jahre hands-on Google Ads im E-Commerce — Shopping, Performance Max und Feed hast du aktuell selbst gesteuert.

  • Du hast schon vier bis fünf Kunden oder Konten parallel eigenverantwortlich betreut, inklusive direkter Kundenkommunikation.

  • Du verfügst über sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse auf C1-Niveau und fühlst dich in Kundengesprächen wohl — auch wenn das Gegenüber fachlich challengt.

  • Du kannst deine Zahlen jederzeit erklären und übernimmst Verantwortung für das Ergebnis.

Das ist ein Plus, aber kein Muss

  • Erfahrung mit Demand Gen oder YouTube

  • Du hast schon mit Scripts, Automatisierung oder AI-Tools gearbeitet — tiefes Tool-Wissen bringen wir dir bei

  • Erfahrung als Mentor:in für Junioren

  • Du wohnst zwischen Flensburg, Kiel und Hamburg

Du hast zwei Jahre Google-Ads-Erfahrung statt drei, aber richtig Bock auf den nächsten Schritt? Melde dich trotzdem — auch dafür sind wir offen.

Die Vorteile für dich

  • Vergütung: 60.000–80.000 € Fixum je nach Level plus 10 % Bonus auf dein Portfolio oberhalb von 30.000 € im Monat — monatlich ausgezahlt, nicht am Jahresende

  • Nur Google Ads: fachliche Tiefe und täglicher Austausch mit vielen Google-Ads-Seniors statt Kanal-Bauchladen

  • Eigenes AI- & Dev-Team: vier Entwickler bauen Tools und Automations für dich — dazu eigenes CSS, Attribution und Budgetsteuerung mehrmals täglich

  • Drei Entwicklungspfade: Experte für DemandGen, Controlling oder AI & Automation, mehr Portfolio-Breite oder Teamlead — Expertenrollen zählen im Bonus mit

  • Remote oder hybrid: zwei Wochen Onboarding in Flensburg, danach kommst du zu Schulungen und Team-Events; Reisen zu Kunden höchstens einmal im Jahr

  • Office mit Fördeblick: Fitnessstudio, Massagen, Bürohunde und freitags Team-Lunch mit eigener Köchin

  • Starke D2C-Marken und Netzwerk: Arbeit für einige der bekanntesten D2C-Brands im deutschsprachigen Raum

Warum du dich jetzt melden solltest

Wenn du Lust hast, in einem Kanal richtig Experte zu sein, ist Touchpoint der richtige Ort. Du bekommst Werkzeuge, die andere Agenturen nicht haben, Kunden, die du selbst führst, und einen Bonus, der jeden Monat zeigt, was du bewegst.

Kontakt

Diese Position wird über A-Level besetzt. Fragen zur Rolle, Vergütung oder zum Prozess gehen direkt an: Sören Gerdes

About this role:

We're hiring an Accounting Operations Manager to own the operational core of fal's finance function: payables, spend management, procurement, and the books of our subsidiaries. You will work in Pacific Standard Time zone, run the weekly cadence that keeps vendors paid and spend under control, and you will turn the processes behind it into documented, audit-ready controls as fal completes its first financial statement audit and moves to a new ERP.

This is a hands-on role for someone who likes building processes as much as running it.

What you’ll do

Spend management and AP oversight

  • Own Ramp administration and allocate and oversee workload carried by offshore supporting AP team

  • Act as the first point of contact for employee and vendor questions on spend, declined transactions, and payment status.

  • Review card transactions and reimbursements for policy compliance, receipt support, GL coding, and accrual cut-off, and follow up on exceptions until they close.

  • Run the weekly payables cycle end to end: invoice intake, matching to PO and receipt, GL and department coding, and approval routing.

  • Maintain the vendor master, including W-9 collection, bank-detail changes verified by call-back, and controls against payment fraud.

  • Prepare the weekly payment batch with a cash-requirements summary for finance leadership approval.

Procurement and purchase orders

  • Collaborate with Finance, Legal, and Ops on scalable procurement processes, including approval thresholds by amount, department, and vendor risk.

  • Partner with Legal and budget owners so contracts, POs, and invoices tie out before payment.

Subsidiary accounting and intercompany

  • Keep the books for fal's subsidiaries under US GAAP, including journal entries, account reconciliations, and monthly close.

  • Record, settle, and reconcile intercompany transactions and balances each month.

  • Prepare elimination entries and support consolidation of entity financials.

  • Bring acquired entities onto fal's chart of accounts, close calendar, and control environment.

Audit readiness and systems

  • Document process narratives and controls for AP, treasury, and procurement, and prepare the evidence auditors request.

  • Help configure AP, procurement, and intercompany workflows in fal's new ERP.

  • Use AI tools and automation to remove manual steps from invoice processing, coding, and reconciliations.

1099 reporting, tax and close support

  • Own 1099 readiness year-round: vendor classification, TIN matching, and complete W-9 and W-8 files.

  • Prepare, review, and approve annual 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC filings, and handle corrections and IRS notices.

  • Support Tax function on ad hoc basis, including sales and use tax, and property tax.

  • Support the month end close process, including but not limited to reconciliations of prepaids, deposits, payables, accruals.

Qualifications/Nice-to-haves

  • 5+ years in accounting operations, accounts payable, or general accounting

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance.

  • Hands-on experience running AP and spend management in Ramp, Brex, or Bill.com, integrated with an ERP.

  • Strong working knowledge of US GAAP, month-end close, and balance sheet reconciliations.

  • Exposure to foreign subsidiaries, multi-currency accounting, or post-acquisition integration.

  • Direct experience preparing and filing 1099s.

  • A track record of designing internal controls: segregation of duties, approval matrices, and audit evidence.

  • Precise and organized, and comfortable owning a recurring cadence with hard deadlines.

  • Clear written communication with vendors, employees, and auditors.

  • Fluency with AI tools and workflow automation to scale finance operations.

  • Experience at a venture-backed, high-growth technology company, ideally through a first audit.

  • CPA, or progress toward licensure.

  • ERP implementation or migration experience (NetSuite, Rillet, or similar).

What we offer at fal

Your Mission:

We are looking for a Senior Weight Management Engineer (all genders) to join our Central Engineering team and lead mass properties engineering activities for the Microliner aircraft. You will be responsible for establishing, maintaining, and communicating the aircraft mass properties baseline throughout the development lifecycle. Working closely with the Overall Aircraft Design, Airframe, Systems, Propulsion, Technology, Flight Physics, and Configuration Management teams, you will guide aircraft, system, and discipline owners in establishing reliable mass data and consolidate this information into a consistent, traceable, and configuration-controlled aircraft mass properties baseline.

As a senior member of Central Engineering, you will provide mass properties expertise across the organization, support technical and programme decision-making, and ensure that mass properties objectives are consistently considered throughout design, verification, certification, and production.

 

Your Day-to-Day:

  • Lead mass properties engineering for the Microliner across aircraft, system, subsystem, and lower levels, ensuring reliable, traceable, and configuration-controlled mass data throughout design maturation, verification, certification, and transition into production.

  • Maintain, further develop, analyse, and communicate the consolidated aircraft mass properties baseline.

  • Manage and continuously refine mass targets, allocations, margins, and weight-saving objectives in collaboration with aircraft, system, and discipline owners.

  • Guide aircraft, system, and discipline owners in estimating, substantiating, and maintaining mass properties data for their respective scope, providing methods, quality assurance, and configuration-control guidance.

  • Perform aircraft weight and balance analyses, including operational loading conditions, centre-of-gravity envelopes, loading scenarios, and compliance with applicable airworthiness requirements.

  • Evaluate mass properties across aircraft configurations, managing applicability, effectivity, and consistency within the aircraft mass model.

  • Assess and communicate the mass-properties impact of design changes, technical trades, system integration decisions, and configuration changes.

  • Define mass properties verification and weighing requirements, and coordinate with suppliers and system owners to ensure that measured data is appropriately substantiated, reconciled, and incorporated into the configuration-controlled aircraft mass properties baseline.

  • Further develop and continuously improve mass properties processes, methods, tools, reporting, governance, and interfaces with configuration management and the wider engineering toolchain.

Your Profile:

  • Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a comparable technical discipline.

  • Minimum 8 years of professional experience in aircraft mass properties engineering, preferably within the development and certification of civil aircraft under EASA CS-23 or FAA Part 23. Relevant experience from CS-25/Part 25, military or eVTOL development is also considered.

  • Experience with the mass properties of battery-electric aircraft, electric propulsion systems, high-voltage systems, or other electric aviation technologies is a strong plus.

  • Demonstrated experience managing aircraft mass properties throughout the product development lifecycle, including mass estimation, target setting, allocation, tracking, reporting, configuration control, and the incorporation of substantiated mass data into the aircraft baseline.

  • Strong expertise in aircraft weight and balance, centre-of-gravity envelope development, loading analysis, moments of inertia, mass margins, uncertainty management, and mass-properties substantiation.

  • Demonstrated experience working across the complete aircraft product hierarchy, from aircraft-level mass objectives and operational loading conditions through system, and lower-level hardware mass data, ensuring consistency and traceability between levels.

  • Good understanding of aircraft design, systems integration, configuration management, certification, and the interaction between mass properties, aircraft performance, structures, stability and control, and operational capability.

  • Proficiency with mass properties databases and analysis tools, as well as experience integrating mass data within product lifecycle management and configuration-controlled engineering environments; experience with Dassault Systèmes 3DEXPERIENCE is a strong plus.

  • Structured, analytical, and solution-oriented professional with strong ownership of aircraft-level outcomes, attention to detail, and the ability to communicate mass properties implications effectively across technical disciplines and programme stakeholders.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English; additional European languages are an asset

  • Strong motivation for aviation and the advancement of electric aircraft technologies.

     

We recognize that women and other under-represented groups are often overlooked in our industry. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every listed qualification, we still encourage you to apply. Talent and potential can’t always be captured in a checklist.

 

Why us?

  • Be part of an ambitious team determined to shape the future of aviation.

  • We are an in-office company, but we value flexibility and trust employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work or adjusting hours to accommodate personal commitments.

  • Subsidized EGYM Wellpass membership: your (mental) health is important for us.

  • Enjoy a subsidized lunch with a 5€ company contribution per meal on office days.

  • Become a part of our success with virtual stock options.

  • Choose the option that suits your needs: either a free charging station for your electric car or a public transport job ticket as part of the Deutschlandticket.

  • Lease a high-quality bicycle or e-bike through our JobRad program and benefit from tax advantages. Whether for your daily commute or personal use, enjoy more mobility and sustainability.

  • Pension scheme to support your long-term financial security.

  • Work in one of our offices in Munich or Delft. Enjoy the modern Balan Campus in Munich or work inside the aerospace ecosystem at TU Delft.

  • Boost your professional as well as personal growth executing your own ideas and independent projects.

  • Join our internal social events and retreats (e.g. cooking, game nights, sports).

VÆRIDION was founded in 2021 to transform regional air travel with the Microliner, a 100% electric commercial aircraft. By delivering the most energy-efficient aircraft, we are building the future where clean, safe, and affordable electric aviation seamlessly connects people and businesses. We’re bringing together the brightest minds in aerospace, automotive engineering, and business to disrupt the aviation industry.

tonies is the world’s leading interactive audio platform for children, with over 12 million Tonieboxes and 173 million Tonies sold globally. Our intuitive, screen-free system empowers children to learn and play independently in a safe and engaging way.

With a presence in over 100 countries and a diverse portfolio of ~1,500 Tonies across multiple languages, we continue to redefine how children experience storytelling and learning. Since our IPO in 2021, our global team of 630+ colleagues is united by a shared mission: shaping the future of play, learning, and imagination.

Team Lead Global Logistics (all genders)

Your Role & Impact

As Head of Fulfillment & Logistics Europe, you will own physical logistics, omnichannel operations, and customer deliveries across all our European markets, including the European logistics network strategy. You will also oversee Channel Operations via the Channel Operations Team Lead, and lead the automation roadmap that underpins our Channel Ops efficiency case.

This role is central to making sure our products reach our customers and retail partners on time, every time, as we scale across Europe. This is a hands-on leadership role: while you will operate at a strategic level with senior stakeholders, you are equally ready to work through operational details yourself when needed, especially as we continue to build out our European team.

What you'll do

  • Lead the European logistics network strategy, ensuring 3PL partners meet SLAs across all markets.

  • Develop the unified European logistics network, warehouse footprint, and 3PL selection.

  • Oversee outbound management and local 3PL performance to ensure “on-time in-full” delivery to warehouses and end customers.

  • Manage the regional Channel Operations team via the Channel Operations Team Lead, including end-to-end order-to-cash management and resolution of customer claims.

  • Own the automation roadmap (EDI, returns automation, reporting, invoicing) unlocking the Channel Ops efficiency target.

  • Review and approve European fulfillment budgets with the Sr. Director Operations Europe.

  • Act as the senior point of contact for complex delivery issues at the European level.

  • Own the budget and strategic resource allocation across the fulfillment and logistics function.

What You Bring

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, or a related field.

  • 8+ years of experience in logistics, fulfillment, or 3PL management, including experience leading a team, ideally across multiple European markets.

  • Proven track record designing or scaling a logistics/warehouse network and managing 3PL partnerships.

  • Experience driving automation or process-efficiency initiatives (e.g. EDI, returns automation).

  • Strong financial acumen and experience managing an operational budget.

  • Excellent stakeholder management skills, comfortable engaging with senior leadership and external partners.

  • Comfortable working both strategically with senior leadership and hands-on with day-to-day fulfillment details, especially given our current team size and growth stage.

  • Fluent in English; additional European languages are a plus.

  • Willing & able to work from our office in Düsseldorf, London, or Paris 2 days a week .

How You Work

  • Hands-on first: Happy to dive into the operational details yourself, while spotting and driving improvements along the way.

  • Commercially minded: Focused on cost efficiency, service quality, and measurable results.

  • Structured and analytical: Data-driven, organized, and solution-oriented.

  • Collaborative leader: Able to lead a small, multidisciplinary team and work effectively across functions.

  • Self-starter: You don't need a long onboarding. You look at how things run, come up with your own ideas (like questioning whether a different port or route would serve us better), align on them and make them happen.

Why Join Us?

  • Global teamwork: We work together across departmental and national borders on our vision of bringing the Toniebox to every child's room in the world.

  • Come as you are: This applies not only to the dress code, but to everything else as well. Because you can only give your best when you feel truly comfortable.

  • Mobility: Choose the offer that best suits you – a Germany ticket for unlimited mobility, a monthly payment of fifty euros for an office parking space, a leased bicycle or a remote work allowance.

  • Protection: Benefit from subsidies for employee savings plans, company pension schemes and disability insurance.

  • Relaxation & Time Out: Enjoy 30 days of paid annual leave plus three additional days off, such as Carnival Monday, Christmas Eve, and New Year's Eve. After one year of employment, you can also take up to 10 "toniecation days" (unpaid leave).

  • Continuous professional development: Benefit from our internal and external training opportunities as well as an individual learning budget to continuously expand your knowledge.

  • Language learning and relaxation made easy: Improve your communication skills with the Babbel language learning app and find relaxation through our access to the Calm meditation app.

  • Discounts: Benefit from attractive discounts on our entire tonies range.

 

As part of our principles, we are committed to supporting inclusion and diversity at tonies. We actively celebrate our colleagues’ different abilities, ethnicities, faith and gender. Everyone is welcome and supported in their development at all stages in their journey with us.

We look forward to hearing from you!

Dabei verbindet das Unternehmen moderne Technologien mit kundenorientierten Prozessen und schafft durchgängige Lösungen, die Unternehmen dabei unterstützen, ihre kaufmännischen Abläufe effizienter zu gestalten. Mit bereits mehr als 2.500 Kunden hat sich das Unternehmen in seinem Heimatmarkt erfolgreich positioniert.

Nach dem erfolgreichen Aufbau im niederländischen Markt möchte POM nun auch in Deutschland weiter wachsen und das kommerzielle Segment gezielt erschließen.   • Sie übernehmen die Verantwortung für die Erschließung und Entwicklung neuer Geschäftsfelder im kommerziellen Marktumfeld von POM in Deutschland.

  • Sie identifizieren die entsprechenden Zielgruppen, Marktsegmente und potenzielle Kunden und entwickeln daraus konkrete Geschäftsmöglichkeiten.

About Us

Constructor is the next-generation platform for search and discovery in ecommerce, built to explicitly optimize for metrics like revenue, conversion rate, and profit. Our search engine is entirely invented in-house utilizing transformers and generative LLMs, and we use its core and personalization capabilities to power everything from search itself to recommendations to shopping agents. Engineering is by far our largest department, and we’ve built our proprietary engine to be the best on the market, having never lost an A/B test to a competitive technology. We’re passionate about maintaining this and work on the bleeding edge of AI to do so.

Out of necessity, our engine is built for extreme scale and powers over 1 billion queries every day across 150 languages and roughly 100 countries. It is used by some of the biggest ecommerce companies in the world like Sephora, Under Armour, and Petco.

We’re a passionate team who love solving problems and want to make our customers’ and coworkers’ lives better. We value empathy, openness, curiosity, continuous improvement, and are excited by metrics that matter. We believe that empowering everyone in a company to do what they do best can lead to great things.

Constructor is a U.S. based company that has been in the market since 2019. It was founded by Eli Finkelshteyn and Dan McCormick who still lead the company today.


The Team

The Core Team sits at the heart of Constructor, shaping Constructor’s in-house search engine, where user requests meet customer catalogs and Constructor’s learnings. We build and operate the foundational systems that power every request flowing through the platform, enabling fast, reliable, and intelligent interactions at massive scale.

Our systems handle billions of requests daily with exceptional uptime, and we take pride in delivering a highly scalable, resilient, and globally distributed platform. As part of the Core team, you will help design, build, and maintain the critical infrastructure and services that underpin the entire product, ensuring performance, stability, and reliability across the globe.


Requirements

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a strong foundation in computer science, including algorithms, data structures, concurrency, and systems design.

  • Have experience building and scaling high-traffic, high-availability backend systems.

  • Have experience designing and operating backend infrastructure, including deployment automation, capacity planning, and observability.

  • Are comfortable working across different layers of the stack, from performance-critical code to production operations.

  • Enjoy learning new technologies and tools in a fast-moving, large-scale environment.

  • Collaborate effectively and contribute to a positive, ownership-driven team culture.

Our Tech Stack

  • Languages: Rust, C++, Python

  • Cloud Infrastructure: AWS

  • CI/CD: Jenkins, GitHub Actions

  • Monitoring & Observability: Prometheus, Grafana


Benefits

  • 🏝️ Unlimited vacation time - we strongly encourage all of our employees take at least 3 weeks per year

  • 🌎 Fully remote team - choose where you live

  • 🛋️ Work from home stipend! We want you to have the resources you need to set up your home office

  • 💻 Apple laptops provided for new employees

  • 🧑‍🎓 Training and development budget for every employee, refreshed each year

  • 👪 Maternity & Paternity leave for qualified employees

  • 🧠 Work with smart people who will help you grow and make a meaningful impact

  • 📈 Stock options - offered in addition to the base salary

  • 🎉 Regular team offsites to connect and collaborate

Compensation

The base salary for this role starts at $80K+ USD for Mid-level and $90K+ USD for Senior. Your starting salary will depend on your experience, skills, and the level we align on during the interview process.

 

🎯 Experience level: We actively recruit Mid-level Engineers and above to support high productivity in our remote-first environment. We are not currently hiring for entry-level or Junior Engineer positions.


Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion at Constructor

At Constructor.io we are committed to cultivating a work environment that is diverse, equitable, and inclusive. As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome individuals of all backgrounds and provide equal opportunities to all applicants regardless of their education, diversity of opinion, race, color, religion, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status or affiliation in any other protected group.

Studies have shown that women and people of color may be less likely to apply for jobs unless they meet every one of the qualifications listed. Our primary interest is in finding the best candidate for the job. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all of our listed qualifications.

How we handle your data. By submitting this application, you acknowledge that Constructor will collect and process the personal data you provide for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for this role. If you are not selected, we will retain your data for a limited period as described in our Recruitment Privacy Notice. After that period your data will be deleted or anonymized.

Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

As Customer Success Leader, you lead the team that is custodian of value for Harvey's Enterprise law-firm customers across Northern Europe. You own gross and net revenue retention across the segment, built on Harvey becoming embedded in how each firm's practice groups work and every firm moving along the AI maturity curve. You will be a visible executive presence with managing partners and firm leadership across a portfolio of prestigious, high-profile firms.

As a member of the broader Customer Success leadership team, you will set the strategy, playbooks and operating rhythm that let every CSM run their book as a portfolio and deliver a consistently high standard for every firm.

Through empathetic leadership and a high bar, you will hire and develop CSMs into trusted advisers to innovation leaders, practice group leaders and managing partners, so partners and associates see undeniable value and each firm builds a lasting AI advantage.

You will also partner across Harvey's go-to-market, product and legal engineering teams to shape how we serve law firms end to end.

What You'll Do

  • Build and lead a high-performing team: hire, coach and develop Enterprise Law Firm CSMs across Northern Europe, promoting a culture of accountability, execution, growth and relentless improvement.

  • Own retention, expansion and renewal readiness: run the segment as a portfolio — knowing, with evidence, whether each firm needs protecting or growing — surface risk early, build expansion plans with Sales where there is room to grow, ensure every firm is multi-threaded, and forecast accurately against gross and net revenue retention targets.

  • Prove value: coach your team to align each firm on measurable outcomes — capacity, realisation, matter economics, client impact — and capture the value stories and ROI evidence that underpin renewal and growth.

  • Lead at partner level: grow CSMs into trusted advisers who cultivate champions and partner sponsors, and engage directly with managing partners, senior partners and innovation leaders at the segment's key firms.

  • Set the standard for the firm's journey: define and scale the playbooks — mutual success plans tied to each firm's objectives, kickoffs, implementation reviews, QBRs and executive business reviews — that take every firm from pilot to daily use, practice group by practice group.

  • Orchestrate cross-functionally: partner with Sales, Legal Engineering, Innovation Partners, the Transformation Office and Product leaders so each firm gets the right expertise at the right moment.

  • Run the product feedback flywheel: turn the voice of law-firm customers into prioritised input for Product and Engineering, and into improvements in how we deliver.


What You Have

Ideal candidates for the Customer Success Leader, Enterprise Law Firms role at Harvey can demonstrate comfort and experience with the following:

  • A proven background leading high-performing Customer Success or account management teams in late-stage or post-IPO enterprise SaaS, serving strategic or lighthouse accounts with substantial six-figure annual spend — ideally law firms or other professional services firms.

  • A track record of owning and delivering a team-level revenue, retention or net-revenue-retention number, with accurate forecasting.

  • Building teams through hiring, coaching and developing talent, with a leadership style grounded in empathy and a high bar.

  • Designing and scaling playbooks that take enterprise customers from initial adoption to embedded, organisation-wide use, with measurable outcomes grounded in concrete use cases.

  • Building multi-threaded relationships at senior level and influencing partners and stakeholders who did not buy the product.

  • Portfolio planning and revenue-based prioritisation across a regional book, including early identification and mitigation of risk.

  • Quantifying and communicating business value and ROI to senior legal stakeholders.

  • An AI-native way of working: you use AI and sophisticated tooling daily, can show how it has changed your own and your team's output, and have a point of view on how AI changes legal practice.

  • Communicating and influencing at every level, internally and externally, including running in-person meetings with managing partners and firm leadership.

  • Law-firm experience is a strong plus: an understanding of how partnerships make decisions, how practice groups differ and what partners, associates and innovation teams each care about, ideally in the Northern European legal market.

  • Adapting seamlessly in the face of high-speed change and growth, with a strong point of view and proactive self-management.

Developers decide what’s interesting long before they decide what to buy. They follow builders, share the talk everyone is watching, and argue about benchmarks in the replies. Most infrastructure brands show up in that feed looking and sounding the same. ClickHouse has the material to do something different: a fast, open-source database that has grown into a platform for real-time analytics, data warehousing, observability, and AI workloads; engineers and leaders with real points of view; and a brand that already turns up in unexpected places, from a Premier League partnership to our own Open House conference.

We are looking for a Senior Social Media Manager to run the ClickHouse accounts and turn that material into a brand developers actually want to follow, at the intersection of infrastructure, technology, and culture. You’ll own our presence on LinkedIn, X, and YouTube with video at the center: clipping talks, podcasts, launches, and live moments into content that travels, building formats people come back for, and working with the creators developers already trust. You’ll be accountable for growing audience and engagement across a global community.

You’ll sit on the Story & Communications team, reporting to the Head of Story & Communications, and work closely with developer relations, product marketing, demand generation, events, and our brand and design team. This is a hands-on role: you’ll make the work, not only schedule it.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Run the ClickHouse accounts on LinkedIn, X, and YouTube end to end: strategy, voice, calendar, publishing, and community management, with an approach built for each channel and for a global audience across time zones

  • Put video at the center of how ClickHouse shows up: clip talks, podcasts, livestreams, launches, and executive moments into short-form and vertical content, and build recurring, social-first series that earn a following

  • Build a brand developers find interesting at the intersection of infrastructure, technology, and culture, pairing technical depth with humor, opinion, and craft

  • Work with the creators and technical voices developers already follow, through collaborations, co-created content, guest appearances, and amplification, in tandem with developer relations and the wider marketing team

  • Turn launches, announcements, customer stories, and research into social moments, and bring live coverage from Open House and industry events, working with regional teams so local moments reach a global audience

  • Grow the voices around the brand: partner with communications on executive presence on LinkedIn and X, and give employees and developer advocates what they need to share their work

  • Own the numbers for organic social, including audience growth, engagement, video performance, and share of the developer conversation, and report on what’s working and why

  • Track what developers say about ClickHouse and the category and feed it back to product marketing, developer relations, and campaign teams, while using AI tooling and a lean production workflow to ship content quickly and partnering with demand generation so the best organic work gets paid reach

What You Bring Along

  • A record of growing audience and engagement at scale for a brand with a global following, and the numbers to show it

  • Real fluency with video: you can shoot, edit, and clip yourself, you know what makes short-form and vertical content work on each platform, and you can find the best ninety seconds in an hour-long talk

  • Experience running influencer or creator programs: finding the right voices, structuring partnerships, and making the collaboration feel native to the creator’s audience

  • Experience with a technical or B2B audience, and the ability to turn technical substance into something people want to share

  • Preferred: experience in SaaS, developer tools, or infrastructure

  • Taste and a point of view on internet culture: you know where developers spend time online, what they find funny, and what makes them tune a brand out

  • Sharp short-form writing: the post, the hook, the caption, the thread

  • A builder’s approach: you test quickly, read the data honestly, scale what works, and drop what doesn’t

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

  • Maintain a UK security risk register covering personnel, physical, information and programme security. Work with Cybersecurity and IT to identify and track relevant cyber risks, and advise or escalate material risks to UK leadership and the Board Level Contact.

Required Qualifications

  • Eight or more years of progressively responsible industrial, government, defence, intelligence, or corporate security experience, including ownership of a UK defence-security programme.

  • Strong leadership, judgement, discretion, writing, and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to translate requirements into practical processes in a fast-paced technology environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Mission

Neko Health is a health technology company that opened its first clinic in Stockholm in 2018, founded by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne.

In one hour, our scan combines radiation-free imaging, heart and circulation measurements, and same-visit blood results with time to talk it through with a clinician, so people can act on what matters before symptoms appear. We design and build our own hardware, software and clinical protocols, and more than 100,000 members have already had a scan, with 75% booking and prepaying their next one before they leave.

As a team, we chase 10X, not 10%, and we’re looking for people who think the same way to help us scale what we’ve started in Sweden, the UK, and now the US. Join the clinicians, engineers and business builders making prevention a routine part of care.

Role Purpose

This is not a traditional laboratory role. We're looking for a Biomedical Scientist who is comfortable working differently, embraces innovation, and takes pride in delivering accurate results at exceptional pace.

Neko Health members come through our clinics for whole-body preventive health screenings, and our laboratories sit at the centre of the patient journey. They are busy, modern spaces, and the service continues to develop as we scale.

This is a hands-on, autonomous role, based on site in one of our central London laboratories. As a Biomedical Scientist, you will operate our Abbott Alinity and Sysmex XN-550 analysers and support the quality systems that allow us to return results within 30 minutes of sample receipt.

If you're a BMS looking to further develop your career in an innovation-led environment, we would love to hear from you.

 

What You'll Deliver in the First 6 - 12 Months

  • Initialise the analysers each day and ready them for sample processing.

  • Perform testing on our Abbott Alinity (biochemistry and immunoassay) and Sysmex XN-550 (haematology) analysers, validating patient results and escalating clinically anomalous or unexpected findings.

  • Carry out daily calibration, internal quality control, and routine maintenance of analysers, troubleshooting and escalating technical issues promptly.

  • Work within our ISO 15189-aligned, UKAS-facing quality management system: author SOP updates, monitor EQA performance, support audits, and investigate non-conformances.

  • Contribute to service improvement work, including analyser verification, reagent evaluation, and software testing.

  • Maintain accurate, auditable records and support performance monitoring across turnaround times, KPIs, and consumables usage.

  • Provide technical guidance to clinical colleagues and support training across the lab team.

 

Minimum Requirements

  • HCPC registration as a Biomedical Scientist, with evidence of ongoing CPD.

  • Minimum one year of post-registration experience in clinical chemistry and immunoassay, including IQC and EQA practice.

  • Demonstrable experience operating an integrated clinical chemistry and immunoassay analyser.

  • Experience working accurately and efficiently under time pressure, suited to a low-volume, fast-turnaround service model.

 

Preferred

  • Post-registration experience in haematology.

  • Hands-on experience operating Sysmex XN-series haematology analysers.

  • Hands-on experience operating Abbott Alinity ci-series.

  • Experience in POCT, rapid diagnostics, or high-throughput clinical settings.

  • Experience with laboratory information management systems (LIMS), digital result reporting, or involvement in LIMS development and user acceptance testing.

About titles at Neko

We use a simplified internal title framework that prioritises clarity over hierarchy, so the title on this posting may differ from your internal title. We’ll be open about the scope and level of the role throughout the process, so you know exactly what you’d be taking on.

Role Purpose

You own the clinical bar across the Neko clinics in the North and Midlands (currently Birmingham and Manchester).

That means every consultation in your area meets the same threshold of safety, quality, and member experience across your region. It means the clinical teams working with you are developing, not just performing. It means clinical issues are being seen and addressed before they show up in audits or member complaints. And it means the quality metrics for your region are known, owned and moving in the right direction. And it means clinical judgment shows up at the table when operational decisions are being made.

You'll partner closely with the UK Medical Director, who holds final clinical authority for the UK market, and operate in true dyad partnership with the Area Clinic Manager for your region who owns the operational side. The clinical health of the region is yours.

What You'll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months

  • Hold the clinical standard across every site in your area

  • Manage and develop the clinicians in your region: performance conversations, development plans, coaching, and the honest feedback that turns good clinicians into great ones.

  • Ensure lead clinicians in your market(s) are performing excellently and that the clinical teams have the appropriate clinical escalation pathways in place.

  • Support clinical hiring for your area against defined criteria, and partner with the Training and Education team to close training gaps as they emerge.

  • Own the review and closure of clinical incidents and near-misses in your area, making sure learnings are actually applied, not just documented.

  • Own the quality metrics for your region: accountable for performance against Neko's medical quality goals at area level, including scan quality (perfect scan score), member follow-up quality and timeliness (perfect follow-up score and follow-up SLAs), clinical safety (Northstar Clinical Safety score) and clinician summary quality and timeliness. Review the data with your Area Clinic Manager each week and month, trace variation to root cause by site and clinician, set improvement actions, and report progress and risks to the UK Medical Director.

  • Operate in true dyad partnership with the Area Clinic Manager: co-owning quality, member experience, and business goals, attending and contributing to Weekly and Monthly Business Reviews, and bringing clinical input into operational decisions before they're made.

  • Round your sites regularly to observe, support, and listen, surfacing what's working so it can spread, and what isn't so it can be addressed.

  • Build and maintain trusted relationships with the GPs, NHS trusts and private specialist clinicians who receive Neko referrals, monitoring referral quality and addressing breakdowns quickly.

  • Know the UK regulatory landscape: CQC registration and inspection standards, GMC/NMC professional standards and revalidation, NHS and GP referral pathways and obligations, and UK-specific clinical rules, and flag emerging risks before they become problems.

  • Lead or participate in clinical pilots as required - defining success, capturing learnings, and documenting outcomes so the rest of the company can learn from your region.

What We're Hiring For

  • Holds the Bar at Scale. You're the kind of clinical leader who can make sure every consultation feels the same regardless of site or clinician, not by micromanaging, but by setting a clear standard, coaching to it, and noticing when it drifts. You're rigorous without being rigid.

  • Develops the Clinicians You Lead. You take clinician development seriously. You give honest feedback even when it's uncomfortable. You spot what someone needs before they ask. You know the difference between a clinician who needs coaching and one who needs to leave, and you don't avoid either conversation.

  • The Dyad That Actually Works. You bring clinical judgment into operational decisions before they're made and you stay constructive when clinical standards and operational targets pull in different directions. When you escalate, it's because something genuinely needs leadership attention, not because you've stopped trying to resolve it locally.

  • Reads the Pattern, Not Just the Report. You don't just review the data. You see what it's telling you. You round your sites and notice things that don't show up in dashboards. When you spot a pattern you trace it to the root cause and you make sure the right people hear about it.

  • Trusted Outside the Walls. The referral network, the regulators, the specialist clinicians who receive Neko members: these relationships sit with you. You represent Neko credibly because you're a credible clinician yourself. People in the local medical community know your name, and when you flag something, they take it seriously.

Minimum Requirements

  • Full GMC registration with a license to practice, in good standing and with a current revalidation, and right to work in the UK.

  • On the GMC GP Register with qualification (CCT or equivalent) in General Practice.

  • 4+ years of medical leadership experience in the UK health system (NHS and/or private sector), including direct management of clinicians.

  • Demonstrated experience holding clinical standards across multiple sites or a large clinical team.

Preferred

  • Experience in preventive care, tech enabled healthcare or longitudinal care models.

  • Experience operating in a clinical-operational dyad structure.

data.description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

About the role

The Inference team builds and runs the systems that serve Mistral's models to the world.

We own the path from a trained model to a response on someone's screen. That includes the APIs and gateway that requests come through, routing and scheduling across our GPU fleet, and the capacity, deployment and operations work that keeps it all running.

Our work serves two groups. Customers need fast, reliable and cost-efficient inference as usage keeps growing. Our researchers rely on the same systems for evaluation, data generation and reinforcement learning, so what we build feeds directly into the next generation of models.

 

What You Will Do

As an Engineer on Inference, you'll build and run the services that sit between our users and our models. The work is close to the product and to the hardware, and the improvements you make show up quickly in latency, reliability, cost and how fast we can ship new models.

Experience with LLM inference is a plus, but it isn't a requirement. We're just as interested in strong Systems Engineers from other backgrounds who are keen to go deep on serving.

A few of the problems our teams work on:

  • Designing and evolving our inference APIs, so model capabilities like tool calling, structured outputs and new modalities are available to developers on launch day.

  • The backend services and gateway every request passes through, from authentication, streaming and rate limiting to usage metering, observability and end-to-end reliability.

  • Routing, load balancing and autoscaling across our clusters, so we absorb traffic spikes without wasting GPUs.

  • Faster, safer rollouts of new models and serving releases.

What We're Looking For

  • Have several years of experience shipping and running backend or distributed systems that serve real production traffic.

  • Write high-quality production code, and are comfortable using AI coding tools without compromising on it.

  • Care about performance and reliability, and enjoy making systems faster, cheaper and more robust.

  • Have led the design of significant systems, making the right trade-offs and seeing them through to production.

  • Raise the bar for the engineers around you through code review, design discussions and mentoring.

  • It’s a plus if you’ve shipped production backend services in Python or Go, or operated Kubernetes and cloud infrastructure at scale

  • Experience with LLM serving engines such as vLLM is a strong plus.

Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

SENIOR SOFTWARE ENGINEER

Catapult is building the future of sports performance technology, with a mission to Unleash the Potential of every athlete and team on earth. We don't just work in the sporting industry; we are actively changing it.  Since 2006, our solutions have been leading the way in sports performance software, science, and data, in a world where 1% can literally mean the difference between winning and losing.

We work with over 5,800 teams around the world, empowering coaches, managers and trainers in premier teams in the NFL, NBA, NHL, MLS, EPL, AFL, NRL, NCAA and more. We provide the information they need to optimize athletes' health, game-day readiness, and performance, as well as in-game tactics.  

Catapult is a sports technology company that empowers professional teams to make data-driven decisions. We deliver health, performance, video, and AI insights from the locker room to competitive environments, ensuring every decision is an opportunity to gain an advantage, sharpen performance, and build lasting success. 

WE WANT PEOPLE WHO ARE PASSIONATE ABOUT SOLVING HARD PROBLEMS

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help build the Perch camera system, 

Based in London (hybrid), you will work across platform, perception, and ML systems. You will help us improve how we collect, process, and analyze performance data at scale, spanning from devices collecting real-time to backend services and ML infrastructure. All of which will have a direct impact on customers and their experiences with the product.

This role suits a strong generalist who has seen many parts of engineering. You might have worked on any of the following: high-throughput systems, computer vision, robotics, ML infrastructure, or other complex applications. Our ideal candidate brings strong engineering judgment, good technical range, and the ability to learn quickly.

You will be hands-on, working in Python and C++ on devices and services in use by our customers every day.

WHAT YOU'LL DO 

  • Design and implement algorithms for 3D object tracking, segmentation, and motion recognition on embedded hardware.
  • Train and iterate on ML models — from dataset curation through training, evaluation, and deployment to edge devices.
  • Help bring ML, computer vision, or signal-processing systems into production with tight performance constraints
  • Build reliable application features and services that customers use in real environments.
  • Analyze production data to find system limits, product issues, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Collaborate closely with the embedded platform team on model optimization and inference performance, and with the applications team on how tracking data becomes product features.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

  • 4+ years of software engineering experience in production systems.
  • Strong skill in Python and backend engineering.
  • Working knowledge of C++ or a strong reason to be effective in performance-critical code.
  • Experience with data-intensive systems, distributed systems, parallel processing, or efficient data pipelines.
  • Exposure to ML, ML infrastructure, signal processing, real-time systems, computer vision, or related applied technical areas.
  • A track record of shipping reliable software, not only prototypes.
  • Strong debugging skills and the ability to find the root cause of complex system behavior.
  • Clear communication and good judgment when tradeoffs are not simple.
  • Curiosity, adaptability, and the desire to learn new technical areas.

Nice to have — and what would make you exceptional:

  • Experience with computer vision, depth cameras, pose estimation, tracking, or 3D data.
  • Experience with ML model deployment, feature pipelines, evaluation systems, or data quality tools.
  • Experience with streaming data, event systems, real-time processing, or low-latency applications.
  • Experience with numerical methods, signal processing, filtering, state estimation, or robotics.

WHAT YOUR SUCCESS WILL LOOK LIKE

  • In 6 months time, you understand the main systems, ship reliable changes, and help improve a meaningful data or product workflow. You give valuable technical input towards solving problems across backend, data, and perception systems.
  • In 12 months time, you have made a measurable impact on system reliability, product capability, or data quality. You own important parts of the architecture and help the team make better technical decisions.

WHY CATAPULT? 

  • We have amazing people. We promise you'll work with some of the most ambitious,  intelligent people in an exciting industry, and do some of the best work of your life.
  • We encourage our people to engage in constructive, open, and honest communication to make Catapult extraordinary. 
  • We work in a collaborative yet challenging environment to consistently improve our performance, which in turn impacts our customers' performance.
  • Our workforce spans more than 20 countries. You'll have the opportunity to work with people from multiple nationalities and cultures, and to build your global awareness.  
  • We value improvement and development. We are challenging ourselves to continuously grow and become a high-performance company. That means we maintain a growth mindset in everything we do, and our people are always looking for ways to improve.  There is an unlimited opportunity to grow, do more, and do better.

Whether you're interested in sports or not, you'll have the satisfaction of knowing your work is supporting some of the most successful teams and athletes on the planet! 

Research shows that while men apply for jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other marginalized groups tend only to apply when they check every box. So if you have what it takes, but don't meet every single point in our job ad, please still get in touch! We would love to have a chat and see if you could be a great addition to our team. We are building the future of sports performance. Our priority is to find the brightest talent who can add to our team culture, actively contribute, and be excited about what they do.

All offers of employment are subject to Catapult's positive prehire check. To find out more, please contact the Talent Partner for this role.

About DataCamp

DataCamp's mission is to empower everyone with the data and AI skills essential for 21st-century success. By providing practical, engaging learning experiences, DataCamp equips learners and organizations of all sizes to harness the power of data and AI. As a trusted partner to over 17 million learners and 6,000+ companies, including 80% of the Fortune 1000, DataCamp is leading the charge in addressing the critical data and AI skills shortage.

About the role

Research has consistently shown that one-on-one tutoring dramatically outperforms traditional classroom instruction—a finding known as Bloom's 2 Sigma Problem. Despite decades of awareness, no solution has successfully delivered personalized tutoring at scale. Until now.

We are building an AI tutoring system designed to emulate and eventually surpass the best human tutors. You will work on the core AI system that delivers real-time, adaptive learning experiences to learners. If you're excited about building the future of human learning, this role is for you. This role can be done remotely from anyone of the following; United Kingdom, Belgium, Portugal OR UAE

About you

At DataCamp, we seek individuals who embody our core values of data-driven decision-making, action, transparency, ownership, and customer focus. You thrive in a fast-paced, high-performing environment and are driven by a passion for making a meaningful impact. You're adaptable, embracing change and ambiguity with enthusiasm. Your initiative and entrepreneurial spirit push you beyond just meeting targets—you aim to understand the "why" behind our goals and take ownership to drive the business forward. You're a collaborative team player who values transparency and always seeks to improve and innovate. If this sounds like you, we encourage you to apply!

Responsibilities

  • Build and evolve the core AI tutoring system, including prompt architectures, agentic workflows, and real-time adaptive behaviors.
  • Run rigorous experimentation and evaluation, developing custom metrics and frameworks to measure learning effectiveness and improve model reliability.
  • Design and implement scalable, maintainable software, integrating AI capabilities with platform systems, content pipelines, and user experience components.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with educators, content creators, and product teams to translate pedagogical goals into technical solutions.
  • Prototype and productionize novel model interactions, leveraging emerging research and capabilities to advance the tutor's intelligence.
  • Ensure quality, safety, and observability through monitoring, testing, guardrails, and iterative refinement of model behavior.
  • Share knowledge and elevate teammates, contributing to a culture of clarity, simplicity, and continuous learning.

Qualifications

Technical

  • 1+ years building complex LLM-based systems, with strong prompt engineering intuition and experience designing agentic workflows.
  • Ability to design meaningful evaluation methods, including custom metrics and frameworks when off-the-shelf options fall short.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals, architectural thinking, and fluency in Python; comfortable working with production infrastructure, cloud environments, and CI/CD.
  • Actively follows AI research and emerging capabilities, applying new ideas creatively to real problems.

Product & Pedagogy

  • Strong empathy for learners and content creators; able to translate pedagogical goals into system behavior and product decisions.
  • Ability to reason holistically across AI behavior, content structure, platform features, and user experience.
  • Familiarity with learning science or a desire to develop expertise.

Character & Collaboration

  • Drawn to difficult, ambiguous problems with no clear blueprint; persistent in exploring and refining solutions.
  • Preference for elegance and simplicity in system design.
  • Communicates clearly across mediums and enjoys mentoring and collaborating in small, high-ownership teams.

Why Datacamp? 

Joining DataCamp means becoming part of a dynamic, creative, and international start-up. Here are just a few of the reasons why you'll love being on our team:

  • Exciting challenges: Face new technical challenges daily, keeping your work engaging and rewarding.
  • Competitive compensation: We offer a competitive salary with attractive benefits.
  • Flexibility: Benefit from flexible working hours because the future is flexible! 
  • Continuous learning: Access a yearly learning budget for conferences & training to support your professional growth.
  • Global retreats: Participate in international company retreats, fostering a global team spirit.
  • Equipment: Yearly refreshment of your IT Equipment budget for your home working setup.
  • Amazing team: Collaborate with a truly exceptional team—seriously, we're awesome!

A little about us

incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Notion, Linear, Ramp and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime.

The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.

We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.

The role in one line

Customers trust us when things go wrong. We're the software reliability platform built to investigate, respond to and prevent incidents. As a Commercial CSM, you're the partner to our mid-market engineering teams - getting them onboarded, embedded and expanding their usage, and maturing their incident management and reliability as they grow.

What that looks like day to day

Our Customer Success organisation is at the heart of incident.io. We're the team closest to our customers' hardest problems, and we're trusted to solve them. We believe in a customer-led product approach, working hand in hand with Product to uncover and address what each customer really needs. Our goal goes beyond satisfaction: we want to delight customers at every stage of their journey, and build long-term relationships grounded in trust, shared success and mutual growth.

You'll look after 70–80 Commercial customers: growth-oriented tech companies, mostly under 1,000 people, between $30k and $150k ARR each. Industry leaders like Vanta, Monday.com and Loom sit in this segment. Some are steady, some are scaling fast, and much of the job is knowing which is which, and what each one needs from you.

Most of your time goes to mid-market customers on our top-tier plan, where you're their dedicated CSM leading onboarding and adoption. You'll blend 1:1 time with scalable programmes to get teams to value quickly: best-practice sessions, end-user training, partnership and roadmap reviews. You'll also cover a subset of smaller customers in a low-touch capacity, leaning on usage data to spot risk and opportunity early.

Day to day, this is a high ownership role. You'll help customers navigate the product, unpick problems when they hit them, and keep everyone pointed at the outcomes their team actually cares about. You are responsible for proactively identifying expansion and upsell opportunities, and partnering with Sales and Expansion Account Managers to grow revenue within your accounts. Internally, you're the voice of the Commercial customer with Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing and Support.

There's still a lot to build and a ton of opportunity for you to shape this segment. The Commercial motion works, but scaling and automating the customer journey is live work we're ramping up now - refining playbooks, automating the repeatable stuff, building the tooling and content that makes a portfolio this size easier to serve. We're AI-forward in how we approach it, so you'd be shaping this rather than inheriting it.

Who you are

  • You've carried a book of 40 to 100+ accounts and worked out how to be present across all of them without going quiet on half.

  • You've sold to, or supported, technical people, whether that's engineering teams, on-call rotations or developer tools. You can hold your own in a technical conversation without needing to escalate every one of them.

  • You've got commercial instincts. You spot the account that's about to double, you know what a growth signal looks like, and you know how to steer a renewal to a good outcome.

  • You know what scaled CS looks like when it's done well. Playbooks, one-to-many programs, AI-assisted workflows. You don't need to have built them from scratch, but you've worked around them enough to have opinions on what you'd do differently.

  • Half-built process doesn't rattle you. You'd rather fix the documentation than complain about it.

  • You actually like being in a room with customers, and you'll get on a plane for the right one.

Supporting you

We work hard and we think life outside work matters just as much. Our benefits pack is built to support both.

  • Private medical insurance. Seriously good cover — we want you and the people you love to be looked after.

  • Competitive annual leave. Showing up at your best requires switching off, and we make sure you have time to do that.

  • First Friday of every month off. Yes, seriously.

  • Enhanced pension. We put real money in, because future-you deserves better than an afterthought.

  • Meaningful equity. We're rapidly scaling, and everyone who helps shape the outcome should share in it.

  • Unlimited AI spend. For everyone, not just engineers. We're all-in on AI across the company, and we expect you to be too.

  • Generous parental leave. The early days with a new baby matter more than anything we're doing here, and we want you to be present for them.

  • Two budgets that have your back. £1000 to invest in your setup, £500 a year to invest in yourself.

Compensation: £85K – £118K • Offers Equity

  • London • £85K – £118K • Offers Equity
